sentences.text: JUDGMENT Being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 15-12-2016 passed in MVC No.484/2015 by the learned III Additional Senior Civil Judge and VII MACT, Davanagere, whereby, a sum of Rs.1,82,000/- (after deducting Rs.50,000/- paid as interim compensation by the KSRTC) was awarded as compensation on account of the death of one Dadapeer in the road traffic accident and directing the 2nd respondent to deposit the same, the 2nd respondent is before this Court in appeal.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge and VII MACT, Davanagere
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case:

The petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 who are the parents and petitioner Nos. 3 and 4 who are the sister and brother of deceased Dadapeer have filed a claim petition before the Tribunal claiming compensation contending that on 01/04/2015 at about 04:45 pm,
Dadapeer was proceeding towards field on motor cycle bearing No KA-17/EL-9719 to bring a stade.

While he was turning his motor cycle NC: 2023:KHC:25320 towards right side near land of Marulasiddappa on HN-4, 1st respondent being driver of KSRTC Bus bearing KA- 17/F-1512 drove same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to motor cycle ridden by Dadapeer & dragged motor cycle along with Dadapeer up to 15 feet.
He suffered grievous injuries over face, forehead, head, left eyebrow etc, shifted to Bhapuji Hospital, Davanagere was died due to injuries suffered in accident.
The petitioners claimed to have spent Rs. 50,000/- towards funeral expenses of Dadapeer.
3. It was further contended that, prior to accident deceased was doing fruits business and earning more than Rs.12,000/- per month.
The petitioners depended on income of deceased for their livelihood.

It was further contended that, the respondent No-1, driver of offending Bus, the respondent No-2, Managing director of KSRTC and the respondent No-3 insurer of offending Bus are liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, they prayed to award adequate compensation.
In response of notice issued by the Tribunal, respondents No-1 & 2 appeared through their respective counsels.
The respondent No-3 did not appear and he was placed exparte.
5. The respondent No-2 filed objections to main petition admitting that, it is owner of Bus bearing KA-17/F- 1512 along with respondent No-3.

Further, stated that jurisdictional police have registered case against respondent No-1 in Crime No 116/2015 but specifically denied the petition averments that the respondent No-1 drove the Bus in rash and negligent manner and dashed to motor cycle of the deceased and dragged him up to 15 feet, the petitioners spent Rs. 80,000/- towards medical expenses.
The respondent No-2 denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.

Inter alia,
contended that, deceased rode motor cycle bearing No KA- 17/EL 9719 with speed, suddenly overtook the lorry and dashed to front left side of Bus and that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of deceased NC: 2023:KHC:25320 himself and not due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No-1.

Without admitting the liability, respondent No-2 has paid interim The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Gulab Jaan on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72120978/
3 compensation of Rs.50,000/- to petitioner No-2 and the same to be adjusted in main award.

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Smt. Gulab Jaan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further contended that deceased was not having valid driving licence, motor cycle was not registered and was not insured with any company and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of deceased himself and there was contributory negligence on his part.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues.
The petitioner No.1 was examined as PW1 and one witness as examined as PW2 and Exs.P1 to 17 were marked in evidence.
On behalf of the respondents, the driver of KSRTC bus was examined as RW1 and Exs.R1 to 3 were marked in evidence.

7. After hearing the arguments by both the sides, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that petitioners are NC: 2023:KHC:25320 entitled for the compensation of Rs.2,31,200/- and awarded the compensation of Rs.1,82,000/- after deducting Rs.50,000/- paid by KSRTC as interim compensation under the following heads:
Loss of future earning Rs. 1,80,000/-
Loss of consortium Rs. 5,000/-
Loss of estate Rs. 2,500/-
Medical expenses Rs. 1,700/-
Towards love and affection Rs. 40,000/-
Funeral expenses Rs. 2,000/-
Total Rs. 2,31,200/-
Rounded off to Rs. 2,32,000/-
8.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the 2nd respondent-KSRTC has approached this Court in appeal.

The KSRTC has contended that the accident was due to the negligence on the part of the deceased Dadapeer and the Tribunal has failed to appreciate this aspect and as such, the impugned judgment is erroneous and the same be set aside.

9. On issuance of notice by this Court, the respondents 1 to 5 appeared through their respective NC:
2023:KHC:25320 counsels and respondent No.6 was deleted as per order dated 16-1-2018.
10. On admitting the appeal, the Tribunal records have been secured and the arguments by the learned counsel for the appellant was heard through video conferencing and perused the Tribunal records.
However, the counsels appearing for the respondent Nos. 1 to 5 remained absent when the matter was taken up for hearing.

11. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant- KSRTC contend that the Tribunal erred in not noticing the fact that the rider of the motor cycle i.e. the deceased himself had contributed the negligence and he had taken right turn to go to his field without seeing the bus.

It is contended that the Tribunal erred in not noticing that no independent evidence is led in to establish the rash and The Divisional Controller vs Smt. Gulab Jaan on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72120978/
4 negligent driving of the bus driver and also that the deceased was a minor and he was not having valid driving licence as well as the insurance to his motor cycle.

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Smt. Gulab Jaan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NC: 2023:KHC:25320 Therefore, it is contended that the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased should have been appreciated by the Tribunal in coming to the conclusion.
12. It is to be noted that the accident had occurred while the deceased was riding his motor cycle towards his right.
A case was registered against the bus driver on the basis of the complaint filed by one Peersab S/o Noorsab,.
The records also reveal that after the investigation the police had filed chargesheet against the bus driver.
This aspect has been admitted by RW1 in the cross- examination.
It is worth to note that after the accident the bus had dragged the motor cycle of the deceased for about 15 feet on the road and the spot mahazar clearly establish the same.
In order to rebut such investigation made by the Investigating Officer, there is nothing else than the self serving testimony of RW1.
It is evident that the deceased was riding the motor cycle and the accident had occurred at about 4.45 p.m. and as such, the visibility was not in question.
It is evident that RW1 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:25320 contend that the accident occurred while the deceased was overtaking a lorry and he came on the wrong side of the road.
There is nothing on record which would establish this aspect.

When the Investigating Officer has found that the negligence was on the bus driver, nothing prevented RW1 to file a complaint or a private complaint if the complaint was not received by police to show that there was no such negligence on his part, but the negligence was on the part of the deceased.
Under these circumstances, no fault can be found with the Tribunal in fastening the actionable negligence on the bus driver.
13. Learned counsel for the appellant- KSRTC also contends that contributory negligence should have been appreciated by the Tribunal.
In view of the fact that the chargesheet has been filed against the bus driver, there is nothing on record which show that investigation papers were not correct.
Simply because the deceased was a minor and was not having valid DL, it cannot be said that there was contributory negligence on the part of the minor - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:25320 deceased.
Hence, fastening of the liability to the entire extent on the KSRTC cannot be disputed.
14. Respondent Nos. 1 to 4 have not filed any appeal assailing the correctness of he quantum of the compensation.

The Tribunal has held that the deceased was less than 18 years of age and therefore,
he cannot be considered to be an earning member.

By applying the structured formula as envisaged for awarding compensation under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, a sum of Rs.2,31,200/-
has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The said quantum is not disputed by the respondent Nos. 1 to 4.
Under these circumstances, the appeal is bereft of any merits and therefore, it do not call for any interference by this Court.
Consequently, the appeal is dismissed.
